subject: Next steps: control-plane residency and BYOK for MedTech AI
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@medtechai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-18T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: control-plane residency and BYOK — quick clarifications

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great walkthrough of MedTech AI's inference workload and where you run PII/PHI processing. I promised a short recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right deployment option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC / on-prem). High level we heard: you need in-region processing for PHI, customer-controlled KMS/HSM (BYOK), and separation between customer data plane and any Redwood-managed multi-tenant control plane.

A couple of clarifiers before we draft an ops-level recommendation:
- Do you require the control plane (APIs that orchestrate model routing, key ops, billing metadata) to be customer-hosted, or is a customer-managed KMS + strict network egress rules sufficient?
- For KV / model caches: is it acceptable for ephemeral KV cache to exist on a shared host if encrypted with a key you control, or must all KV state persist only on customer-owned network/instances?
- Any strict audit-log retention or granularity (per-request, per-token) requirements beyond the standard 13 months?

I'll pull Ben in on the technical options; Marissa will follow on procurement/contract path if we land on Dedicated or Private. Attached is a quick control-matrix we use to map controls to deployment options — will tailor it once I get your answers.

Next steps proposal:
1) You answer the three clarifying bullets above
2) Ben will propose a minimal architecture for Dedicated vs Private with tradeoffs and estimated lead times
3) Marissa will propose preliminary commercial terms for a pilot (30–90 day)

If you prefer a short 30-minute follow-up call later this week we can do that too.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Redwood_Dedicated_vs_VPC_ControlMatrix.xlsx

From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@medtechai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedTech AI Procurement <procurement@medtechai.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: control-plane residency and BYOK — quick clarifications

Soojin,

Appreciate the recap — that matrix will be helpful. Quick answers inline: 
- Control plane: we cannot allow core orchestration APIs to persist metadata outside our environment. In short, we need the control plane to be resident inside our VPC (Private control plane) or deployed on-prem. A customer-managed KMS alone is not sufficient for us.
- KV cache: ephemeral KV on shared hosts is acceptable only if the cache is always encrypted with keys we control (BYOK with HSM-backed keys), and keys are rotated on our schedule.
- Audit logs: we need per-request audit events (timestamp, requester id, model version, tokens in/out) retained 24 months for compliance.

Additional notes: we ingest PHI/radiology metadata and the legal team insists on no cross-tenant metadata persistence — meaning no shared indexing of prompts or usage signals that are accessible to other customers.

Can you confirm whether Private control plane + Private compute (your on-prem appliance or VPC deployment with private control plane) can meet all of the above? Also, please attach SOC2 and any evidence of HSM integration capabilities. Procurement wants a control-matrix mapping controls to deployment and residual risks.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Stone
Head of Infrastructure & Security
MedTech AI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@medtechai.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: control-plane residency and BYOK — quick clarifications

Hi Emily — thanks for the clarity, this helps a lot. Short answer: yes, we can support a private control plane in-region + HSM-backed BYOK and meet the 24-month per-request audit retention, but there are tradeoffs and lead times to be aware of. Below is a compact mapping and a few technical constraints so procurement can assess residual risk.

Option A — Private VPC (control plane deployed into your VPC)
- Control plane residency: customer-hosted control plane (private control plane) deployed into your VPC via secure peering or private link. Orchestration metadata stays in your environment.
- Compute: Dedicated capacity (GPU pools) can be deployed in the same VPC or in an adjacent customer-dedicated subnet to avoid cross-tenant noisy neighbors.
- KMS/HSM: BYOK supported; we can integrate with your cloud KMS (Cloud HSM) for token and cache encryption keys. Keys never leave your KMS.
- KV cache behavior: We can mount encrypted ephemeral storage tied to your key; if you require sticky persistence it can be configured onto customer-managed instances.
- Audit logs: per-request events delivered to your logging endpoint (e.g., CloudWatch/Stackdriver) with 24-month retention configured on your side.
- Expected lead time: 6–10 weeks (deployment + validation + security review).

Option B — On-prem appliance (air-gapped / on-prem packaged deployment)
- All control and compute within your datacenter; full custody.
- BYOK/HSM: direct HSM integration available; we can support FIPS/HSM modules you require.
- Audit: local collection and retention fully under your ops.
- Expected lead time: 12–16 weeks (packaging, ops runbook, onsite validation).

Constraints / residual items to note:
- Our hosted telemetry (for support) can be disabled; we provide sanitized health endpoints for incident diagnosis but full debug traces require a support agreement and explicit snapshot exports.
- Backups/snapshots of models and KV must be configured; if retention in our managed storage is unacceptable we can redirect snapshots to your S3.
- SLA variation: Dedicated in-VPC with private control plane has the same latency profile as our hosted product but requires network peering; on-prem incurs ops variability.

Attached: I put the initial control-matrix and our most recent SOC2 report for procurement. I'll coordinate with Marissa on the pilot commercial terms.

If this looks good, propose a follow-up call Monday to walk procurement and cloud security through the integration checklist.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOC2_Report_2025.pdf, Redwood_Dedicated_vs_VPC_ControlMatrix.xlsx

Subject: Re: Follow-up: control-plane residency and BYOK — quick clarifications

Ben, Soojin — thanks, that mapping and the timelines are exactly what procurement/security wanted to see. Next items from our side: 
1) Please send a control-matrix where the "residual risk" column is explicitly filled (we need that as part of our vendor risk intake).
2) Confirm whether support/debug snapshots can be redacted automatically (no prompt text) unless we explicitly enable full traces for a support ticket.
3) Marissa — once you have a pilot SOW & pricing placeholder we can route to procurement for an initial PO. Procurement will also request a short statement of work for the 6–10 week private VPC pilot (milestones: deploy control plane, connect KMS, run 72h load test, compliance handoff).

From a channel perspective we prefer Private VPC (control plane in our environment) to start; if that proves operationally heavier we may evaluate on-prem for long-term. For now please treat Private VPC as the recommended path and start drafting the SOW.

Emily
Emily Stone
Head of Infrastructure & Security
MedTech AI
